cultivar: Chinary and clonal bushes of the Darjeeling type
processing: Orthodox black tea made in flushes like Darjeeling: a long wither, gentle rolling, partial oxidation for the spring teas and fuller oxidation in summer and autumn, then firing; certified organic.
harvest_season: March to November in flushes; the first (March–April) and second (May–June) flushes are prized, autumn lots are softer and cheaper.
appearance_dry: Twisted leaf in olive, brown and silver, like a Darjeeling.
taste_profile: Floral and fruity with a honeyed sweetness and a brisk finish; often a little softer and cleaner than a Darjeeling from the same season.

brewing.notes: Brew like a Darjeeling: just under 90 °C, no milk, a second steep for a good lot.

vintage_note: Sold by flush and year under the 'Temi Tea' name, through the garden's own outlets, Indian retailers and the auction system, with first flush on sale from April and second flush from July; grades follow the Darjeeling codes (FTGFOP1 and so on). A few speciality importers carry it abroad. Best within a year of picking.
description:
Temi is the single tea garden of Sikkim, the small Himalayan state between Darjeeling and Bhutan, and its tea is essentially a Darjeeling made just across the border: the same Chinary and clonal bushes, the same flush system, the same light spring style, grown on the slopes above Namchi. The garden was planted in 1969 under the last Chogyal (king) of Sikkim and is still run by the state government.

Manufacture is orthodox: a long wither, gentle rolling, partial oxidation for the spring teas and fuller oxidation in summer and autumn, then firing. The garden is certified organic and markets itself heavily on that.

The cup is bright gold to amber, floral and fruity with a honeyed sweetness and a brisk finish, often a little softer and cleaner than a Darjeeling from the same season. Brew it like a Darjeeling: water around 90 °C, three to four minutes, no milk, a second steep for a good lot.

It is sold by flush and year under the 'Temi Tea' name, both through the garden's own outlets and through the auction system, with first flush on sale from April and second flush from July; a few speciality importers carry it abroad. Grades follow the Darjeeling codes (FTGFOP1 and so on). Drink it within a year of picking.

It is a good choice if you want Darjeeling character at a slightly lower price, and a nice answer to the question of whether the Darjeeling name is about the place or the style.
sources_note: Native name given in Nepali (the main language of Sikkim). The 'Temi Tea Garden' Wikipedia article also exists and could be used instead of 'Sikkim tea'.
